narrative:
The model predicts an 85% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, the time you have spent in your current role, and whether you have received other job offers. 

Your 6–10 years of total experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter experience (half have only 1–5 years), your mid-level tenure aligns more with people who eventually move on. Similarly, having spent 1–5 years in this organization also contributed to the “will leave” direction. This length of time in one workplace is common among those who start looking elsewhere. Finally, the fact that you have received other job opportunities strongly increased the likelihood of departure. Most employees who are expected to stay (77%) have not received outside offers, so this factor weighed heavily against you.

Taken together, these elements created a clear picture for the model that you are at a natural point to consider new horizons. 

The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You may want to reflect on whether staying longer could still align with your plans or if exploring those external opportunities makes more sense. Addressing this now could either change your path or allow a smooth transition. (248 words)
